sn9.13:0.2: On one occasion a number of bhikkhus were dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.13:0.3: They were restless, puffed up, personally vain, rough-tongued, rambling in their talk, muddle-minded, without clear comprehension, unconcentrated, scatter-brained, loose in their sense faculties.
sn9.13:1.1: Then the devatā that inhabited that woodland thicket, having compassion for those bhikkhus, desiring their good, desiring to stir up a sense of urgency in them, approached them and addressed them with verses:
sn9.13:2.1: In the past the bhikkhus lived happily,
sn9.13:2.3: Without wishes they sought their alms,
sn9.13:2.4: Without wishes they used their lodgings.
sn9.13:2.6: They made an end to suffering.
sn9.13:3.1: But now like headmen in a village
sn9.13:3.2: They make themselves hard to maintain.
sn9.13:3.3: They eat and eat and then lie down,
sn9.13:4.2: I here speak only about some:
sn9.13:5.1: My statement is made with reference
sn9.13:5.2: To those who dwell in negligence.
sn9.13:5.3: As for those who dwell in diligence,
sn9.13:5.4: To them I humbly pay homage.
sn9.13:6.1: Then those bhikkhus, stirred up by that devatā, acquired a sense of urgency.
